2169: A planet's value (−45 to 100%) depends on its gravity, temperature and radiation relative to your race's ranges. At 100%, a world holds one million inhabitants. Growth is strong while the planet is sparsely populated, then slows down; beyond capacity, the population dies off. Resources come from the population and the factories it operates.
2171: Ironium, boranium and germanium are extracted by mines according to the planet's concentration, which slowly declines. Ships and installations consume them.
2172: Consumption depends on mass (ships and cargo), engine and speed. Each year a ship travels the square of its Warp in light-years. Ships refuel automatically over a friendly station with a shipyard. Ramscoops recover a little fuel along the way. In the fleet's gauge, the hatched part shows what the route will consume (until the next refuel); it turns red if the tank won't last. Out of fuel, a ship crawls along at Warp 1: the fleet panel shows consumption and remaining fuel on arrival at each waypoint, and speed is lowered automatically if there isn't enough fuel.

2234: Select one of your fleets, click a foreign fleet, then “Intercept”. Since the enemy's destination is never known, the meeting point is calculated from the observed trajectory: it is the first end-of-year position your fleet can reach in time. It stops there and waits. The order is a standing one: the point is recalculated every year as long as the target stays visible, and once it is less than a year away, your fleet heads straight for it. Combat only takes place if one side attacks the other.
2236: A fleet that is nearly out of fuel, crawling along at Warp 1 or 2, shows “Refuel fleet” when one of your idle fleets has fuel to spare. That fleet works out a rendezvous on the stranded fleet's route, gives it what it can while keeping enough to get back, then returns to the nearest shipyard; the refueled fleet sets off again at its best speed.
